}}In 2018, the [[The Wall Street Journal|''Wall Street Journal'']] analysed German crime statistics for crime suspects and found that the foreigners, overall 12.8% of the population, make up a disproportionate share of crime suspects (34.7%) in 2017.<ref name="wsj20181016">{{Cite news|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/ethnic-crime-families-provoke-german-crackdown-1539604801|title=An Ice-Cream Truck Slaying, Party Drugs and Real-Estate Kings: Ethnic Clans Clash in Berlin's Underworld|last=Pancevski|first=Bojan|date=2018-10-15|work=The Wall Street Journal|access-date=2018-10-16|language=en-US|issn=0099-9660|archive-date=20 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181020110450/https://www.wsj.com/articles/ethnic-crime-families-provoke-german-crackdown-1539604801|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2017, as in previous years German citizens constituted the largest group of suspects in organised crime trials. The fraction of non-German citizen suspects increased from 67.5% to 70.7% while the fraction of German citizens decreased correspondingly. For the German citizens, 14.9% had a different citizenship at birth.<ref name="bka_ok_2017_p13">{{Cite web|url=https://www.bka.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/DE/Publikationen/JahresberichteUndLagebilder/OrganisierteKriminalitaet/organisierteKriminalitaetBundeslagebild2017.html;jsessionid=A99EC3231788A672D2AEA397F21B1FEC.live2302?nn=27988|title=BKA - Bundeslagebilder Organisierte Kriminalität - Bundeslagebild Organisierte Kriminalität 2017|website=www.bka.de|page=13|language=de|access-date=2018-08-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180811162834/https://www.bka.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/DE/Publikationen/JahresberichteUndLagebilder/OrganisierteKriminalitaet/organisierteKriminalitaetBundeslagebild2017.html;jsessionid=A99EC3231788A672D2AEA397F21B1FEC.live2302?nn=27988|archive-date=2018-08-11}}</ref>

According to statistics collected by the German Federal Criminal Police Office (BKA), the number of immigrants suspects of sexual offenses in Germany has gone up in absolute numbers, while simultaneously the number of German perpetrators has gone down.<ref name="spiegel_fact_check_2018">{{Cite news|url=http://www.spiegel.de/international/germany/is-there-truth-to-refugee-sex-offense-reports-a-1186734.html|title=Fact-Check: Is There Truth To Refugee Rape Reports?|date=2018-01-17|work=Spiegel Online|access-date=2019-01-13|archive-date=11 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190111100913/http://www.spiegel.de/international/germany/is-there-truth-to-refugee-sex-offense-reports-a-1186734.html|url-status=live}}</ref> At least one immigrant was identified as a suspect in 3404 sexual offense cases in 2016, which were twice as many as the previous year.<ref name="spiegel_fact_check_2018" />

From 2016 to 2017, the number of crimes committed by foreigners in Germany decreased from {{Val|950000}} to {{Val|700000}}, a 23% reduction. According to Interior Minister [[Horst Seehofer]], the reduction was largely due to fewer illegal immigrants arriving or remaining in the country.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.dw.com/en/crime-rate-in-germany-lowest-since-1992-but-seehofer-still-issues-stern-warning/a-43697232?maca=en-Twitter-sharing|title=Crime rate in Germany lowest since 1992, but Seehofer still issues stern warning|date=2018-05-08|website=Deutsche Welle|language=en|access-date=2018-06-18|archive-date=18 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180618230846/http://www.dw.com/en/crime-rate-in-germany-lowest-since-1992-but-seehofer-still-issues-stern-warning/a-43697232?maca=en-Twitter-sharing|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/donad-trump-germany-crime-rate-immigrants-migrants-refugees-a8404786.html|title=Why Donald Trump is wrong about Germany's crime rate|work=The Independent|access-date=2018-06-18|language=en-GB|archive-date=18 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180618200837/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/donad-trump-germany-crime-rate-immigrants-migrants-refugees-a8404786.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://edition.cnn.com/2018/06/18/politics/german-crime-rate-trump-immigration/index.html|title=Trump falsely claims rising German crime rate as he pushes immigration debate|first=Betsy|last=Klein|work=CNN|access-date=2018-06-18|archive-date=18 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180618230554/https://edition.cnn.com/2018/06/18/politics/german-crime-rate-trump-immigration/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Deutsche Welle|DW]] reported in 2006 that in Berlin, young male immigrants are three times more likely to commit violent crimes than their German peers. Hans-Jörg Albrecht, director of the Max Planck Institute for Foreign and International Criminal law in Freiburg, stated that the "one over-riding factor in youth crime [was] peer group pressure."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dw.de/dw/article/0,,1953916,00.html|title=Identifying the Roots of Immigrant Crime|work=DW.COM|access-date=31 July 2012|archive-date=24 February 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240224084647/https://www.dw.com/en/identifying-the-roots-of-immigrant-crime/a-1953916|url-status=live}}</ref> Whereas the [[Gastarbeiter]] in the 50s and 60s did not have an elevated crime rate, second- and third-generation of immigrants had significantly higher crime rates.<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://www.rsf.uni-greifswald.de/fileadmin/mediapool/lehrstuehle/harrendorf/Germany_youngMig.pdf|title = Migration and ethnic minorities in Germany: impacts on youth crime, juvenile justice and youth imprisonment|last=Dünkel|first=Frieder|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160128113053/https://www.rsf.uni-greifswald.de/fileadmin/mediapool/lehrstuehle/harrendorf/Germany_youngMig.pdf|archive-date=28 January 2016}}</ref>

=== Greece ===
{{Further|Immigration to Greece|Crime in Greece}}

Illegal immigration to Greece has increased rapidly over the past several years{{when|date=June 2020}}. Tough immigration policies in Spain and Italy and agreements with their neighboring African countries to combat illegal immigration have changed the direction of African immigration flows toward Greece. At the same time, flows from Asia and the Middle East—mainly Pakistan, Afghanistan, Iraq, and Bangladesh—to Greece appear to have increased as well.<ref name="migrationinformation.org" /> By 2012, it was estimated that more than 1 million illegal immigrants entered Greece.<ref name="migrationinformation.org">{{cite web|url=http://www.migrationinformation.org/Profiles/display.cfm?ID=884|title=Greece: Illegal Immigration in the Midst of Crisis|work=migrationpolicy.org|access-date=17 May 2013|archive-date=2 December 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131202200805/http://www.migrationinformation.org/Profiles/display.cfm?ID=884|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="bbc.co.uk">{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-radio-and-tv-19269891|title=Greeks confront crime wave amid austerity|work=BBC News|date=16 August 2012|access-date=21 June 2018|archive-date=9 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210509062245/https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-radio-and-tv-19269891|url-status=live}}</ref> The evidence now indicates that nearly all illegal immigration to the European Union flows through the country's porous borders. In 2010, 90 percent of all apprehensions for unauthorized entry into the European Union took place in Greece, compared to 75 percent in 2009 and 50 percent in 2008.<ref name="migrationinformation.org" />

In 2010, 132,524 persons were arrested for "illegal entry or stay" in Greece, a sharp increase from 95,239 in 2006. Nearly half of those arrested (52,469) were immediately deported, the majority of them being Albanians.<ref name="migrationinformation.org" /> Official statistics show that immigrants are responsible for about half of the criminal activity in Greece.<ref name="bbc.co.uk"/>

=== Ireland ===
Foreigners are under-represented in the Irish prison population, according to 2010 figures.<ref name=":34" />

=== Italy ===
{{Further|Immigration to Italy|Crime in Italy}}A 2023 study of Italian towns found the immigration did not increase the probability of crime occurring, just the perception that residents were in more danger of crime, especially when migrants were more culturally distant.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bove |first1=Vincenzo |last2=Elia |first2=Leandro |last3=Ferraresi |first3=Massimiliano |date=2023-02-22 |title=Immigration, Fear of Crime, and Public Spending on Security |url=https://academic.oup.com/jleo/article/39/1/235/6423595 |journal=The Journal of Law, Economics, and Organization |language=en |volume=39 |issue=1 |pages=235–280 |doi=10.1093/jleo/ewab021 |issn=8756-6222|hdl=10281/459061 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>
According to the [[Institute for International Political Studies|ISPI]], the Italian prison population in 2018 counted {{Val|59655}} and of those 34% were foreigners, with the largest groups coming from Morocco ({{Val|3751}}), Albania ({{Val|2568}}), Romania ({{Val|2561}}), Tunisia ({{Val|2070}}) and Nigeria ({{Val|1453}}).<ref name=":59">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ispionline.it/en/pubblicazione/jihadist-radicalization-italian-prisons-primer-22401|title=Jihadist Radicalization in Italian Prisons: A Primer|last=ispisito|date=2019-02-28|website=ISPI|language=en|access-date=2019-03-20|archive-date=9 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190309151440/https://www.ispionline.it/en/pubblicazione/jihadist-radicalization-italian-prisons-primer-22401|url-status=live}}</ref> A study of [[immigration to Italy]] during the period 1990–2003 found that the size of immigrant population is positively correlated with the incidence of most types of crime, as well as with the overall number of criminal offenses. However, the causal effect seems limited to some categories of crime: murders, robberies and, to a lesser extent, thefts.<ref name=":21" /> Over the period 2007–2016, the crime rate among non-Italians decreased by around 65%.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://blogs.lse.ac.uk/europpblog/2018/03/03/has-immigration-really-led-to-an-increase-in-crime-in-italy/|title=Has immigration really led to an increase in crime in Italy?|date=2018-03-03|work=EUROPP|access-date=2018-04-12|language=en-US|archive-date=12 April 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180412011201/http://blogs.lse.ac.uk/europpblog/2018/03/03/has-immigration-really-led-to-an-increase-in-crime-in-italy/|url-status=live}}</ref>

A study of Italy before and after the January 2007 European Union enlargement found that giving legal status to the previously illegal immigrants from the new EU members states led to a "50 percent reduction in [[recidivism]]".<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|title = Legal Status and the Criminal Activity of Immigrants|journal = American Economic Journal: Applied Economics|pages = 175–206|volume = 7|issue = 2|doi = 10.1257/app.20140039|first1 = Giovanni|last1 = Mastrobuoni|first2 = Paolo|last2 = Pinotti|year = 2015| hdl=2318/1689095 |url = http://repository.essex.ac.uk/12757/1/Mastrobuoni%26Pinotti%282014%29AEJAE.pdf|access-date = 18 August 2019|archive-date = 24 February 2021|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20210224135217/http://repository.essex.ac.uk/12757/1/Mastrobuoni%26Pinotti(2014)AEJAE.pdf|url-status = live}}</ref> The authors find that "legal status... explains one-half to two-thirds of the observed differences in crime rates between legal and illegal immigrants".<ref name=":0" /> A study on the 2007 so-called "click day" amnesty for undocumented immigrants in Italy found that the amnesty reduced the immigrant crime rate.<ref name=":22" /> The authors estimate "that a ten percent increase in the share of immigrants legalized in one region would imply a 0.3 percent reduction in immigrants' criminal charges in the following year in that same region".<ref name=":22" /> Research shows that stricter enforcement of migration policy leads to a reduction in the crime rate of undocumented migrants.<ref>{{Cite journal|title = Immigration Enforcement and Crime|journal = American Economic Review|pages = 205–209|volume = 105|issue = 5|doi = 10.1257/aer.p20151040|first = Paolo|last = Pinotti|year = 2015|url = https://www.aeaweb.org/aer/ds/10505/P2015_1040_ds.zip|access-date = 4 September 2020|archive-date = 20 September 2015|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150920073813/https://www.aeaweb.org/aer/ds/10505/P2015_1040_ds.zip|url-status = live}}</ref>

According to the latest report by Idos/Unar, immigrants made up 32,6% of prison population in 2015 (four percentage points less than five years before),<ref>{{Cite web|title = Gli stranieri? Delinquono di meno e commettono reati meno gravi degli italiani|url = http://www.redattoresociale.it/Notiziario/Articolo/493497/Gli-stranieri-Delinquono-di-meno-e-commettono-reati-meno-gravi-degli-italiani|website = Redattore Sociale|access-date = 2016-01-17|language = it-IT|archive-date = 6 January 2016|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160106075340/http://www.redattoresociale.it/Notiziario/Articolo/493497/Gli-stranieri-Delinquono-di-meno-e-commettono-reati-meno-gravi-degli-italiani|url-status = live}}</ref> immigrants making up 8,2% of population in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Indicatori demografici|url = http://www.istat.it/it/archivio/149003|website = www.istat.it|date = 12 February 2015|access-date = 2016-01-17|archive-date = 15 November 2017|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20171115202434/http://www.istat.it/it/archivio/149003|url-status = live}}</ref> Prison population data may not give a reliable picture of immigrants' involvement in criminal activity due to different bail and sentencing decisions for foreigners.<ref name=":22" /> Foreigners are, for instance, far more overrepresented in the prison population than their share of convictions relative to the native population.<ref name=":22" /> According to a 2013 study, the majority of foreign prisoners are held in connection with a drug offence.<ref name="ItalyPenal" /> One out of every nine offences ascribed to foreign prisoners concerns violation of 'laws governing foreigners'.<ref name="ItalyPenal" /> The 2013 study cites literature that points to discriminatory practices against foreigners by Italian law enforcement, judiciary and penal system.<ref name="ItalyPenal" />

According to a 2013 report, "undocumented immigrants are responsible for the vast majority of crimes committed in Italy by immigrants... the share of undocumented immigrants varies between 60 and 70 percent for violent crimes, and it increases to 70–85 for property crime. In 2009, the highest shares are in burglary (85), car theft (78), theft (76), robbery (75), assaulting public officer / resisting arrest (75), [[handling stolen goods]] (73)."<ref name=":22">{{Cite web|url = http://www.frdb.org/upload/file/Report%201.pdf|title = Immigration policy and crime|date = 2013|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160202205357/http://www.frdb.org/upload/file/Report%201.pdf|archive-date = 2016-02-02|via=Fondazione Rodolfo Debenedetti}}</ref> The 2013 report observes that "immigrants accounted for almost 23 percent of the criminal charges although they represented only 6‐7 percent of the resident population" in 2010.<ref name=":22" />

According to 2007 data, the crime rate of legal immigrants was 1.2–1.4% whereas the crime rate was 0.8% for native Italians. The overrepresentation is partly due to the large number of young legal immigrants, the crime rate is 1.9% for legal immigrants aged 18–44 whereas it is 1.5% for their Italian peers; 0.4% for legal immigrants aged 45–64 years whereas it is 0.7% for their Italian peers; and for those over 65 years old, the crime rates is the same among natives and foreigners. 16.9% of crimes committed by legal immigrants aged 18–44 are linked to violations of immigration laws. By excluding those crimes, the crime rate of legal immigrants aged 18–44 is largely the same as that of same aged Italians.<ref>{{Cite web|title = La criminalità degli immigrati, indagine "contro corrente"|url = http://www.redattoresociale.it/Notiziario/Articolo/274795/La-criminalita-degli-immigrati-indagine-contro-corrente|website = Redattore Sociale|access-date = 2016-01-17|language = it-IT|archive-date = 2 February 2016|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160202080101/http://www.redattoresociale.it/Notiziario/Articolo/274795/La-criminalita-degli-immigrati-indagine-contro-corrente|url-status = live}}</ref>

A 2016 report by {{ill|Confcommercio|it}} found that between 2010 and 2014, illegal immigrants committed crimes at approximately 57 times the rate of Italians, and 29 times the rate of other foreigners, though it also found that immigration reduces the crime rate when it is characterized by participation and integration.<ref name="n097">{{cite web | title=UNA NOTA DESCRITTIVA SU CRIMINALITÀ E IMMIGRAZIONE | website=confcommercio.it | date=2018-09-14 | url=http://www.confcommercio.it/documents/10180/3599445/Nota+descrittiva+su+criminalit%C3%A0%20e+immigrazione/dcd0881d-e752-430e-9f03-2efb5fdef9eb | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180210030659/http://www.confcommercio.it/documents/10180/3599445/Nota+descrittiva+su+criminalit%C3%A0%20e+immigrazione/dcd0881d-e752-430e-9f03-2efb5fdef9eb | archive-date=2018-02-10 | access-date=2024-09-25 | quote=In summary: the calculations carried out lead to the statement that, approximately and on average, the crime rates for Italians, 10 resident foreigners and irregular foreigners are, for the 12 crimes considered, equal to 4.3, 8.5, 246.3 per 1,000 people of the reference population, respectively. In other words, the propensity to commit crime among irregular persons is approximately 57 times that of Italians and almost 29 times that of regular foreigners (who therefore commit crimes twice as often as Italians) ... }}</ref>

===Netherlands===
{{Further|Immigration to the Netherlands}}
''[[Allochtoon]]'' Dutch youths, especially young [[Demographics of the Netherlands Antilles|Antillean]] and [[Surinamese people in the Netherlands|Surinamese]] [[Rotterdam]]mers, are more often suspected of crime by the police than other youths. More than half of [[Moroccans in the Netherlands|Moroccan-Dutch]] male youths aged 18 to 24 years in Rotterdam have ever been suspected of crimes by the police, while among Netherlands-born youth aged from 18 to 24, 18% have been in contact with the judiciary.<ref name=":60">{{cite web|url=http://www.rijnmond.nl/nieuws/04-06-2009/veel-jonge-criminele-allochtonen-rotterdam|title=Veel jonge criminele allochtonen in Rotterdam|work=RTV Rijnmond|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130102061404/https://www.rijnmond.nl/nieuws/04-06-2009/veel-jonge-criminele-allochtonen-rotterdam|archive-date=2013-01-02}}</ref><ref name=":61">{{cite web|url=http://www.elsevier.nl/web/Nieuws/Nederland/236094/Schokkende-cijfers-criminaliteit-Marokkanen-Rotterdam.htm|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130222175101/http://www.elsevier.nl/web/Nieuws/Nederland/236094/Schokkende-cijfers-criminaliteit-Marokkanen-Rotterdam.htm|archive-date=2013-02-22|title=Schokkende cijfers criminaliteit Marokkanen Rotterdam|work=Elsevier}}</ref> According to a 2009 report commissioned by Justice Minister [[Ernst Hirsch Ballin]], 63% of the 447 teenagers convicted of serious crime are children of parents born outside the Netherlands. All these cases concern crime for which the maximum jail sentence is longer than eight years, such as robbery with violence, extortion, arson, public acts of violence, sexual assault, manslaughter and murder. The ethnic composition of the perpetrators was: native Dutch – 37%; Moroccans – 14%; Unknown origin – 14%; "other non-Westerners" – 9%; Turkish – 8%; Surinamese – 7%; Antillean – 7%; and "other Westerners" – 4%.<ref name=":10">{{Cite web|title=Two out of Three Serious Teenage Criminals are Immigrants |url=http://www.nisnews.nl/public/180309_1.htm |date=2013-02-08 |access-date=2016-01-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130208101230/http://www.nisnews.nl/public/180309_1.htm |archive-date=February 8, 2013 }}</ref>  In the majority of cases, the judges did not consider the serious offences to be grave enough to necessitate an unconditional jail sentence.<ref name=":10" />

Analysis of police data for 2002 by ethnicity showed that 37.5 percent of all crime suspects living in the Netherlands were of foreign origin (including those of the second generation), almost twice as high as the share of immigrants in the Dutch population. The highest rates per capita were found among first and second generation male migrants of a non‐Western background. Of native male youths between the ages of 18 and 24, in 2002 2.2% were arrested, of all immigrant males of the same age 4.4%, of second generation non-Western males 6.4%. The crime rates for so‐called 'Western migrants' were very close to those of the native Dutch. In all groups, the rates for women were considerably lower than for men, lower than one percent, with the highest found among second generation non‐western migrants, 0.9% (Blom et al. 2005: 31).<ref name=":63">{{Cite book|url = https://openaccess.leidenuniv.nl/bitstream/handle/1887/16374/Leun%20van%20der.pdf?sequence=2|isbn = 978-90-5850-573-6|title = Transnational Criminology Manual Volume I|chapter = Immigration, Crime and Criminal Justice Systems|year = 2010|pages = 659–673|publisher = Wolf Legal Publishers|access-date = 5 December 2012|archive-date = 10 October 2013|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20131010143938/https://openaccess.leidenuniv.nl/bitstream/handle/1887/16374/Leun%20van%20der.pdf?sequence=2|url-status = live}}</ref>

For Moroccan immigrants, whether they originate from the underdeveloped parts of Morocco has a modest impact on their crime rate. One study finds that "crime rates in the Netherlands are higher among Moroccans who come from the countryside and the [[Rif]], or whose parents do, than among those who come from the urban provinces in Morocco and from outside the Rif, or whose parents do."<ref>{{Cite journal|title = Crime among young Moroccan men in the Netherlands: Does their regional origin matter?|journal = European Journal of Criminology|volume = 13|issue = 3|date = 2015-12-31|issn = 1477-3708|article-number = 1477370815623566|doi = 10.1177/1477370815623566|language = en|first1 = Frank|last1 = Bovenkerk|first2 = Tineke|last2 = Fokkema|hdl = 20.500.11755/7f0bfbf5-f5c4-43e4-a3bc-3df69a0364b8|s2cid = 54945638|url = http://repub.eur.nl/pub/79763|hdl-access = free|access-date = 22 February 2019|archive-date = 13 July 2019|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190713153836/https://repub.eur.nl/pub/79763|url-status = live}}</ref> In 2015, individuals with a Moroccan background were, not taking their age into account, almost six times as likely to be suspected for a crime compared to the native Dutch. Of the first generation 2.52% was suspected of a crime, of the second generation 7.36%, of males 7.78% and women 1.34%.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.cbs.nl/-/media/_pdf/2016/47/ji2016s_web.pdf|title=Annual Report on Integration 2016|publisher=Statistics Netherlands|year=2016|location=The Hague|page=15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180504191046/https://www.cbs.nl/-/media/_pdf/2016/47/ji2016s_web.pdf|archive-date=4 May 2018}}</ref>

Using 2015 data, [[Statistics Netherlands]] concluded that non-Western male immigrant youths had been relatively often suspected of a crime: 5.42% in the group aged between 18 and 24, compared with 1.92% for native Dutch of the same age. For both male and female non-Western immigrants of all ages combined the numbers were 2.4% for the first generation and 4.54% for the second. The absolute crime rate had dropped by almost a half since the early twenty-first century, for both native Dutch and non-western immigrants.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.cbs.nl/-/media/_pdf/2016/47/ji2016s_web.pdf|title=Annual Report on Integration 2016|publisher=Statistics Netherlands|year=2016|location=The Hague|pages=14–15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180504191046/https://www.cbs.nl/-/media/_pdf/2016/47/ji2016s_web.pdf|archive-date=4 May 2018}}</ref> A study found the estimated security costs per person due to the costs of criminal justice for prosecution, trial and prison attributed to the number of persons at each stage<ref name="x069">{{cite web | title= Technical Appendix to the second edition of the report Borderless Welfare State The Consequences of Immigration for Public Finances, Jan H. van de Beek, Hans, Roodenburg, Joop Hartog, Gerri W. Kreffer, 2023, Demo-Demo publisher, Section 5.2 Security| url=https://demo-demo.nl/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/Borderless_Welfare_State_Technical_Appendix-2.pdf | access-date=13 August 2024}}</ref> showed in 2016 large differences with the region of origin of immigrants, with low security costs on average for immigrants from Scandinavia, United Kingdom, Indonesia and East Asia.<ref name="z370">{{cite report | first1=Jan H. | last1=van de Beek | first2=Hans | last2=Roodenburg | first3=Joop | last3=Hartog | first4=Gerrit W. | last4=Kreffer | ISBN=978-90-833348-2-0 | title=Borderless Welfare State: The Consequences of Immigration for Public Finances | url=https://demo-demo.nl/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/Borderless_Welfare_State-2.pdf | date=2023}}</ref> In 2017, a study concluded that asylum seekers in the Netherlands were less criminal than native Dutch with the same combination of age, gender and socio-economic position.<ref name=":64">Achbari, W., Leerkes, A.S., 2017, ''Van perceptie naar feit — Asielzoekers en buurtcriminaliteit'' WODC, Cahiers 2017-16</ref>

===Norway===

===Spain===
{{Further|Immigration to Spain|Crime in Spain}}{{Primary sources section
| date = July 2024
}}
A 2008 study finds that the rates of crimes committed by immigrants are substantially higher than nationals.<ref name=":20">{{Cite journal|title = Immigration and Crime in Spain, 1999–2006|url = https://ideas.repec.org/p/fda/fdaddt/2008-34.html|publisher = FEDEA|date = 2008-01-01|first1 = Cesar|last1 = Alonso|first2 = Nuno|last2 = Garoupa|first3 = Marcelo|last3 = Perera|first4 = Pablo|last4 = Vazquez|journal = Working Papers|access-date = 26 January 2016|archive-date = 3 February 2016|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160203002056/https://ideas.repec.org/p/fda/fdaddt/2008-34.html|url-status = live}}</ref>{{Better source needed|reason=The current source is insufficiently reliable ([[WP:NOTRS]]).|date=July 2024}} The study finds that "the arrival of immigrants has resulted in a lack of progress in the reduction of offences against property and in a minor increase in the number of offences against Collective Security (i.e. drugs and trafficking). In the case of nationals, their contribution to the increase in the crime rate is primarily concentrated in offences against persons."<ref name=":20" />{{Better source needed|reason=The current source is insufficiently reliable ([[WP:NOTRS]]).|date=July 2024}} By controlling for socioeconomic and demographic factors, the gap between immigrants and natives is reduced but not fully. The authors also find "that a higher proportions of American, non-UE European, and African immigrants tend to widen the crime differential, the effect being larger for the latter ones".<ref name=":20" />{{Better source needed|reason=The current source is insufficiently reliable ([[WP:NOTRS]]).|date=July 2024}} The same paper provides supports for the notion that labour market conditions impact the relationship between crime and immigration. Cultural differences were also statistically detected.<ref name=":20" />{{Better source needed|reason=The current source is insufficiently reliable ([[WP:NOTRS]]).|date=July 2024}} This study has been criticized for not using strong instruments for identifying causality: the "instruments (lagged values of the covariates and measures of the service share of GDP in a province) are not convincing in dealing with the endogeneity of migrant location choice."<ref>{{Cite book|chapter = Immigration and crime|title = International Handbook on the Economics of Migration|pages = 353–372|doi = 10.4337/9781782546078.00028|first1 = Brian|last1 = Bell|first2 = Stephen|last2 = Machin |isbn = 978-1-78254-607-8 | date= 2013 | series= Economics 2013 | editor1=  Amelie F. Constant | editor2= Klaus F. Zimmermann}}</ref> [[Spanish National Statistics Institute]] (INE) published a study that analyzes records in the Register of Convicted in 2008. The data show that immigrants are overrepresented in the crime statistics: 70% of all crimes were committed by Spaniards and 30% by foreigners.<ref name="tercerainformacion.es">{{cite web|url=https://www.tercerainformacion.es/antigua/?article10906|title=El 70% de la delincuencia es perpetrada por españoles según el INE|work=tercerainformacion.es|access-date=11 March 2020|archive-date=8 March 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210308224236/https://www.tercerainformacion.es/antigua/?article10906|url-status=live}}</ref> Foreigners make up 15% of the population.<ref name="tercerainformacion.es" />{{Better source needed|reason=The current source is insufficiently reliable ([[WP:NOTRS]]).|date=July 2024}}

===Sweden===
{{Further|Immigration to Sweden|Crime in Sweden}}[[File:Share of 15yo+ immigrant and descendant crime suspects by region 2015-2018 - BRÅ.png|thumb|312x312px|Data source: [[Swedish National Council for Crime Prevention|Swedish National Council of Crime Prevention]] (Swedish: ''Brottsförebyggande Rådet'' or BRÅ)]]
Those with immigrant background are over-represented in Swedish crime statistics. Research shows that socioeconomic factors, such as unemployment, poverty, exclusion, language, and other skills explain most of difference in crime rates between immigrants and natives.<ref name=":12" /><ref name=":11" /><ref name=":36">{{Cite news |last=Skodo |first=Admir |date=2017-03-01 |title=Why Swedish immigration is not out of control: Sweden's crime rate is not affected by the immigration rate and the state has introduced stricter asylum laws |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/politics/swedish-immigration-is-not-out-of-control-it-s-actually-getting-more-restrictive-a7605071.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170820042949/http://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/politics/swedish-immigration-is-not-out-of-control-it-s-actually-getting-more-restrictive-a7605071.html |archive-date=20 August 2017 |access-date=2017-04-02 |work=The Independent |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name=":41">{{Cite news |last1=Ahlander |first1=Johan |last2=Johnson |first2=Simon |date=2017-02-21 |title=Sweden - not perfect, but not Trump's immigrant-crime nightmare |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-sweden-crime-trump-idUKKBN16024W |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170706171400/http://www.reuters.com/article/uk-sweden-crime-trump-idUKKBN16024W |archive-date=6 July 2017 |access-date=2017-04-02 |work=Reuters}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Noack |first=Rick |date=February 20, 2017 |title=Analysis {{!}} Trump asked people to 'look at what's happening ... in Sweden.' Here's what's happening there. |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/worldviews/wp/2017/02/20/trump-asked-people-to-look-at-whats-happening-in-sweden-heres-whats-happening-there/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170403111841/https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/worldviews/wp/2017/02/20/trump-asked-people-to-look-at-whats-happening-in-sweden-heres-whats-happening-there/ |archive-date=3 April 2017 |access-date=2017-04-02 |newspaper=Washington Post}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2017-02-20 |title=After Trump comments, the reality of crime and migrants in Sweden |url=http://www.france24.com/en/20170220-after-trump-comments-reality-crime-migrants-sweden |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170410051503/http://www.france24.com/en/20170220-after-trump-comments-reality-crime-migrants-sweden |archive-date=10 April 2017 |access-date=2017-04-09 |work=France 24 |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2022, Annika Lindberg of the [[University of Gothenburg]] said that in Sweden there has been a "sort of merging of migration and crime in discourse" even though there is "no sort of research showing that there exists such a causal kind of relationship."<ref name=":57">{{Cite news |last=Davis Jr. |first=Elliott |date=December 30, 2022 |title=Sweden, Once Welcoming to Immigrants, Changes Course |url=https://www.usnews.com/news/best-countries/articles/2022-12-30/sweden-once-welcoming-to-immigrants-shifts-course |work=US News and World Report |quote=On a similar note, there are the issues around how migration is discussed in the country, especially by followers of the Sweden Democrats. Specifically, there has been a 'sort of merging of migration and crime in discourse' even though there is 'no sort of research showing that there exists such a causal kind of relationship,' says Annika Lindberg, a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Gothenburg's School of Global Studies. In 2017, for example, Sweden's Ministry of Foreign Affairs had to distribute a press release providing facts and context to combat the dissemination of 'simplistic and occasionally inaccurate information about migration, integration and crime' in the country.}}</ref><ref name=":56">{{Cite news |last=Valverde |first=Miriam |date=February 20, 2017 |title=Facts on Sweden, immigration and crime |url=http://www.politifact.com/truth-o-meter/article/2017/feb/20/what-statistics-say-about-immigration-and-sweden/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170224170008/http://www.politifact.com/truth-o-meter/article/2017/feb/20/what-statistics-say-about-immigration-and-sweden/ |archive-date=24 February 2017 |access-date=2017-04-02 |work=PolitiFact |language=en |quote='In general, crime statistics have gone down the last (few) years, and no there is no evidence to suggest that new waves of immigration has led to increased crime,' Selin said.}}</ref>

According to the vice [[National Police Commissioner (Sweden)|National Police Commissioner]] of the Swedish Police Authority, intelligence gathered by police showed that there are about 40 ethnic crime clans in Sweden who came to the country in order to pursue organized crime. They are primarily settled in Stockholm, Södertälje, Gothenburg, Malmö, Landskrona and Jönköping. In these clans, the extended family raises the children to take over the organized crime activities and they have no ambitions to become integrated into Swedish mainstream society.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Polischefen: "40 släktbaserade kriminella nätverk i Sverige"|url=https://www.expressen.se/nyheter/polischefen-40-slaktbaserade-kriminella-natverk-i-sverige/|access-date=2020-09-06|website=www.expressen.se|date=5 September 2020 |language=sv|archive-date=6 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200906051029/https://www.expressen.se/nyheter/polischefen-40-slaktbaserade-kriminella-natverk-i-sverige/|url-status=live}}</ref> Swedish prime minister [[Stefan Löfven]] had long denied that crime gangs had anything to do with immigration, but in September 2020 changed his stance in an SVT interview, where he said that a large immigration led to difficulties with integration which in turn increased risk of crime.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Zangana|first=Beri|date=2020-09-09|title=Löfvens vändning: Kopplar ihop stor migration med brottsutvecklingen|language=sv|work=SVT Nyheter|url=https://www.svt.se/nyheter/inrikes/lofven-ser-sociala-spanningar|access-date=2020-09-21|archive-date=15 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200915150346/https://www.svt.se/nyheter/inrikes/lofven-ser-sociala-spanningar|url-status=live}}</ref>

About one third of new prison inmates in the 2011–2019 did not have Swedish citizenship, where there was an increase in the share from 29% in 2011 to 33% in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|title=KOS 2019 - Kriminalvård och statistik (PDF download)|url=https://www.kriminalvarden.se/om-kriminalvarden/publikationer/kartlaggningar-och-utvarderingar/kos-2019---kriminalvard-och-statistik/|access-date=2020-10-10|website=Kriminalvården|page=32|language=sv|archive-date=2020-10-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201013050357/https://www.kriminalvarden.se/om-kriminalvarden/publikationer/kartlaggningar-och-utvarderingar/kos-2019---kriminalvard-och-statistik/}}</ref> A 2014 survey of several studies found that people with foreign background are, on average, two times more likely to commit crimes than those born in Sweden. This figure has remained stable since the 1970s, despite the changes in numbers of immigrants and their country of origin.<ref>{{cite book|author=Amber Beckley, Johan Kardell and Jerzy Sarnecki|title=The Routledge Handbook on Crime and International Migration|pages=46–47|publisher=[[Routledge]]}}</ref> Some studies{{which|date=April 2019}} reporting a link on immigration and crime have been criticized for not taking into account the population's age, employment and education level, all of which affect level of crime. In general, research that takes these factors into account does not support the idea that there is a link between immigration and crime.<ref>{{cite book|author=Amber Beckley, Johan Kardell and Jerzy Sarnecki|title=The Routledge Handbook on Crime and International Migration|page=42|publisher=[[Routledge]]}}</ref>

==== Recent immigration to Sweden ====
Crime and immigration was one of the major themes of the [[2018 Swedish general election]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/03/03/world/europe/sweden-crime-immigration-hand-grenades.html|title=Hand Grenades and Gang Violence Rattle Sweden's Middle Class|first1=Ellen|last1=Barry|first2=Christina|last2=Anderson|work=The New York Times|date=3 March 2018|access-date=2018-08-15|language=en|archive-date=7 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180807205040/https://www.nytimes.com/2018/03/03/world/europe/sweden-crime-immigration-hand-grenades.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/aug/14/swedish-pm-asks-arsonists-what-the-heck-are-you-doing-setting-fire-to-cars|title='What the hell are you up to?' Arson attacks draw Swedish PM's ire|last=Crouch|first=David|date=2018-08-14|website=The Guardian|language=en|access-date=2018-08-15|archive-date=12 February 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190212161108/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/aug/14/swedish-pm-asks-arsonists-what-the-heck-are-you-doing-setting-fire-to-cars|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2018, Swedish Television investigative journalism show Uppdrag Granskning analysed the total of 843 [[District courts of Sweden|district court]] cases from the five preceding years and found that 58% of all convicted of rape had a foreign background and 40% were born in the [[Middle East]] and [[Africa]], with young men from [[Afghanistan]] numbering 45 stood out as being the most next most common country of birth after Sweden. When only analysing rape assault (Swedish: ''överfallsvåldtäkt'') cases, that is cases where perpetrator and victim were not previously acquainted, 97 out of 129 were born outside Europe.<ref name="svt_2018_rapists">{{Cite news|url=https://www.svt.se/nyheter/granskning/ug/ny-kartlaggning-av-valdtaktsdomar-58-procent-av-de-domda-fodda-utomlands|title=Ny kartläggning av våldtäktsdomar: 58 procent av de dömda födda utomlands|last=Nyheter|first=SVT|date=2018-08-22|work=SVT Nyheter|access-date=2018-08-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180822190937/https://www.svt.se/nyheter/granskning/ug/ny-kartlaggning-av-valdtaktsdomar-58-procent-av-de-domda-fodda-utomlands|archive-date=22 August 2018|publisher=[[Swedish Television]]/[[Uppdrag Granskning]]|language=sv}}</ref>

Viral falsehoods have circulated in recent years that tie immigrants and refugees to an alleged surge of crime in Sweden.<ref name=":42">{{Cite news|url=http://www.factcheck.org/2017/02/trump-exaggerates-swedish-crime/|title=Trump Exaggerates Swedish Crime - FactCheck.org|date=2017-02-20|work=FactCheck.org|access-date=2017-04-02|language=en-US|archive-date=24 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170224114559/http://www.factcheck.org/2017/02/trump-exaggerates-swedish-crime/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/sweden-refugees-trump-crime-rape-2017-2?r=US&IR=T/|title=Trump again slammed Sweden's immigration policies at CPAC 2017 — here's what's really going on|work=Business Insider|access-date=2017-04-02|language=en|archive-date=30 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170930082807/http://uk.businessinsider.com/sweden-refugees-trump-crime-rape-2017-2?r=US&IR=T/#doubt-over-the-fox-news-segment-1|url-status=live}}</ref> According to [[Jerzy Sarnecki]], a criminologist at [[Stockholm University]], "What we're hearing is a very, very extreme exaggeration based on a few isolated events, and the claim that it's related to immigration is more or less not true at all."<ref name=":42" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/opinion/swedens-rape-crisis-isnt-what-it-seems/article30019623/|title=Sweden's rape crisis isn't what it seems|work=The Globe and Mail|access-date=2017-04-02|language=en-ca|archive-date=17 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170817162117/https://www.theglobeandmail.com/opinion/swedens-rape-crisis-isnt-what-it-seems/article30019623/|url-status=live}}</ref> A 2020 pan European comparative study conducted by the Swedish National Council for Crime Prevention showed that if reported and cleared rapes are measured in a comparable way, the number of rapes in Sweden are close to the European average.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.bra.se/download/18.7d27ebd916ea64de5306c65f/1601393665407/2020_13_Reported_and_cleared_rapes_in_Europe.pdf|title=Reported and cleared rapes in Europe: Difficulties of international comparisons|publisher=[[Swedish National Council for Crime Prevention]]|date=October 2020|page=94|access-date=4 November 2020|archive-date=5 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201005034817/https://www.bra.se/download/18.7d27ebd916ea64de5306c65f/1601393665407/2020_13_Reported_and_cleared_rapes_in_Europe.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref> According to Klara Selin, a sociologist at the National Council for Crime Prevention, the major reasons why Sweden has a higher rate of rape than other countries is due to the way in which Sweden documents rape ("if a woman reports being raped multiple times by her husband that's recorded as multiple rapes, for instance, not just one report") and a culture where women are encouraged to report rapes.<ref name=":42" /> Stina Holmberg at the National Council for Crime Prevention, noted that "there is no basis for drawing the conclusion that crime rates are soaring in Sweden and that that is related to immigration".<ref name=":41" />

In 2017, FactCheck.Org noted that "experts&nbsp;said there is no evidence of a major crime wave."<ref name=":42" /> According to official statistics, the reported crime rate in Sweden has risen since 2005 whereas annual government surveys show that the number of Swedes experiencing crime remain steady since 2005, even as Sweden has taken in hundreds of thousands of immigrants and refugees over the same period.<ref name=":39">{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-trump-sweden-idUSKBN15Y0QH|title=Trump baffles Sweden with crime comment, says it was based on TV report|date=2017-02-19|work=Reuters|access-date=2017-02-20|archive-date=6 July 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170706033607/http://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-trump-sweden-idUSKBN15Y0QH|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bra.se/bra/brott-och-statistik/brottsutvecklingen.html|title=Brottsutvecklingen|website=BRÅ.se|access-date=5 April 2017|archive-date=28 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170228051919/http://bra.se/bra/brott-och-statistik/brottsutvecklingen.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/monkey-cage/wp/2017/02/24/no-sweden-isnt-hiding-an-immigrant-crime-problem-this-is-the-real-story/|title=Analysis {{!}} No, Sweden isn't hiding an immigrant crime problem. This is the real story.|newspaper=Washington Post|access-date=2017-04-09|archive-date=7 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170407231639/https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/monkey-cage/wp/2017/02/24/no-sweden-isnt-hiding-an-immigrant-crime-problem-this-is-the-real-story/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.smh.com.au/world/the-swedish-migrant-crime-story-that-donald-trump-didnt-tell-20170225-gul5s6.html|title=The Swedish migrant crime story that Donald Trump didn't tell|last=Miller|first=Nick|date=2017-02-25|work=The Sydney Morning Herald|access-date=2017-04-09|language=en-US|archive-date=11 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190611154328/https://www.smh.com.au/world/the-swedish-migrant-crime-story-that-donald-trump-didnt-tell-20170225-gul5s6.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.politico.com/story/2017/02/trump-sweden-twitter-235196|title=Trump's 'Last night in Sweden' comment fuels Twitter firestorm|work=Politico|access-date=2017-04-10|archive-date=11 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170411054836/http://www.politico.com/story/2017/02/trump-sweden-twitter-235196|url-status=live}}</ref> Jerzy Sarnecki, a criminologist at the University of Stockholm, said foreign-born residents are twice as likely to be registered for a crime as native Swedes but that other factors beyond place of birth are at play, such as education level and poverty, and that similar trends occur in European countries that have not taken in a lot of immigrants in recent years.<ref name=":40">{{Cite news |last=Hjelmgaard |first=Kim |date=February 21, 2017 |title=Sweden to Trump: Immigrants aren't causing a crime wave |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/world/2017/02/21/sweden-migrants-trump/98187090/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170403121927/https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/world/2017/02/21/sweden-migrants-trump/98187090/ |archive-date=3 April 2017 |access-date=2017-04-02 |work=USA Today |language=en}}</ref>

According to data gathered by Swedish police from October 2015 to January 2016, 5,000 police calls out of 537,466 involved asylum seekers and refugees.<ref name=":43">{{Cite news|url=https://www.dn.se/nyheter/sverige/ett-fatal-brott-i-sverige-kopplas-till-flyktingar/|title=Ett fåtal brott i Sverige kopplas till flyktingar|date=2016-02-09|work=[[Dagens Nyheter]]|access-date=2017-04-02|language=sv-se|archive-date=15 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170415192055/http://www.dn.se/nyheter/sverige/ett-fatal-brott-i-sverige-kopplas-till-flyktingar/|url-status=live}}</ref> According to Felipe Estrada, professor of criminology at [[Stockholm University]], this shows how the media gives disproportionate attention to and exaggerates the alleged criminal involvement of asylum seekers and refugees.<ref name=":43" /> Henrik Selin, head of the Department for Intercultural Dialogue at the [[Swedish Institute]], noted that allegations of a surge in immigrant crime after the intake of more than 160,000 immigrants in 2015 have been "highly exaggerated... there is nothing to support the claim that the crime rate took off after the 160,000 came in 2015." While it's true that immigrants have been over-represented among those committing crimes—particularly in some suburban communities heavily populated by immigrants, he said—the issue of crime and immigration is complex.<ref name=":42" /> Speaking in February 2017, Manne Gerell, a doctoral student in criminology at [[Malmö University]], noted that while immigrants where disproportionately represented among crime suspects, many of the victims of immigrant crimes were other immigrants.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2017/02/20/world/europe/trump-pursues-his-attack-on-sweden-with-scant-evidence.html|title=From an Anchor's Lips to Trump's Ears to Sweden's Disbelief|last1=Baker|first1=Peter|date=2017-02-20|work=The New York Times|access-date=2017-04-02|last2=Chan|first2=Sewell|issn=0362-4331|archive-date=25 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211225182204/https://www.nytimes.com/2017/02/20/world/europe/trump-pursues-his-attack-on-sweden-with-scant-evidence.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

A Swedish Police report from May 2016 found that there have been 123 incidents of sexual molestation in the country's public baths and pools in 2015 (112 of them were directed against girls). In 55% of cases, the perpetrator could be reasonably identified. From these identified perpetrators, 80% were of foreign origin.<ref>https://polisen.se/Global/www%20och%20Intrapolis/%C3%96vriga%20rapporter/Lagesbild%20over%20sexuella%20ofredanden.pdf {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170411150139/https://polisen.se/Global/www%20och%20Intrapolis/%C3%96vriga%20rapporter/Lagesbild%20over%20sexuella%20ofredanden.pdf |date=11 April 2017 }} (page 15, section 3.8.1.5)</ref> The same report found 319 cases of sexual assault on public streets and parks in 2015. In these cases, only 17 suspected perpetrators have been identified, 4 of them Swedish nationals with the remainder being of foreign origin. Another 17 were arrested, but not identified.<ref>https://polisen.se/Global/www%20och%20Intrapolis/%C3%96vriga%20rapporter/Lagesbild%20over%20sexuella%20ofredanden.pdf {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170411150139/https://polisen.se/Global/www%20och%20Intrapolis/%C3%96vriga%20rapporter/Lagesbild%20over%20sexuella%20ofredanden.pdf |date=11 April 2017 }} (page 11, section 3.8.1.2)</ref>

In March 2018, newspaper [[Expressen]] investigated [[Gang rape|gang]] [[Rape in Sweden|rape]] court cases from the two preceding years and found that there were 43 men having been convicted. Their average age was 21 and 13 were under the age of 18 when the crime was committed. Of the convicted, 40 out of the 43 were either immigrants (born abroad) or born in Sweden to immigrant parents.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.expressen.se/nyheter/brottscentralen/qs/de-ar-mannen-som-valdtar-tillsammans/|title=De är män som våldtar kvinnor tillsammans: "Jag tyckte det var en rolig grej att filma"|work=Expressen|access-date=2018-03-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180320113923/https://www.expressen.se/nyheter/brottscentralen/qs/de-ar-mannen-som-valdtar-tillsammans/|archive-date=20 March 2018|language=sv-SE}}</ref> Another investigation by newspaper Aftonbladet found that of 112 men and boys convicted for gang rape since July 2012, 82 were born outside Europe. The median age of the victims was 15, while 7 out of 10 perpetrators were between 15 and 20.<ref name=":51">{{Cite news|url=https://www.aftonbladet.se/nyheter/a/rLKwKR/unik-granskning-112-pojkar-och-man-domda-for-gruppvaldtakt|title=112 pojkar och män dömda för gruppvåldtäkt|work=Aftonbladet|access-date=2018-05-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180507070557/https://www.aftonbladet.se/nyheter/a/rLKwKR/unik-granskning-112-pojkar-och-man-domda-for-gruppvaldtakt|archive-date=7 May 2018|language=sv}}</ref> According to professor Christian Diesen, a foreigner may have a lower threshold to commit sexual assault due to having grown up in a misogynist culture where all women outside the home are interpreted as available. Also professor Henrik Tham stated that there was a clear over-representatation of foreigners and cultural differences, while also adding that few cultures allow such behaviour. Professor [[Jerzy Sarnecki]] instead emphasized socioeconomic factors and that police may be more diligient in investigating crimes by foreigners.<ref name=":51" />

A 2024 study by [[Lund University]] found that nearly two thirds of convicted rapists in Sweden since 2000 were first or second generation immigrants.<ref name="b660">{{cite web | last=Rothwell | first=James | title=Nearly two thirds of convicted rapists in Sweden are migrants or second generation immigrants | website=The Telegraph | date=2025-01-18 | url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/world-news/2025/01/18/nearly-two-thirds-convicted-rapists-sweden-migrants/ | access-date=2025-01-23}}</ref>

==== Past immigration to Sweden ====
A 2005 study by the Swedish National Council for Crime Prevention found that people of foreign background were 2.5 times more likely to be suspected of crimes than people with a Swedish background, including immigrants being four times more likely to be suspected of for lethal violence and robbery, five times more likely to be investigated for sex crimes, and three times more likely to be investigated for violent assault.<ref name=":16">{{Cite web|title = Brottslighet bland personer födda i Sverige och i utlandet - Brå|url = https://www.bra.se/bra/publikationer/arkiv/publikationer/2005-12-14-brottslighet-bland-personer-fodda-i-sverige-och-i-utlandet.html|website = www.bra.se|access-date = 2016-01-26|language = sv|archive-date = 17 January 2016|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160117174321/http://www.bra.se/bra/publikationer/arkiv/publikationer/2005-12-14-brottslighet-bland-personer-fodda-i-sverige-och-i-utlandet.html|url-status = live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thelocal.se/20051214/2683|title=Immigrants behind 25% of Swedish crime|work=thelocal.se|date=14 December 2005 |access-date=7 December 2013|archive-date=15 December 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131215170401/http://www.thelocal.se/20051214/2683|url-status=live}}</ref> The report was based on statistics for those "suspected" of offences. The Council for Crime Prevention said that there was "little difference" in the statistics for those suspected of crimes and those actually convicted.<ref name=":16" /> A 2006 government report suggests that immigrants face discrimination by law enforcement, which could lead to meaningful differences between those suspected of crimes and those actually convicted.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Är rättvisan rättvis? Tio perspektiv på diskriminering av etniska och religiösa minoriteter inom rättssystemet|url = http://www.regeringen.se/rattsdokument/statens-offentliga-utredningar/2006/03/sou-200630/|website = Regeringskansliet|date = 2006-03-16|access-date = 2016-01-26|language = sv|first = Regeringen och|last = Regeringskansliet|archive-date = 4 February 2016|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160204162624/http://www.regeringen.se/rattsdokument/statens-offentliga-utredningar/2006/03/sou-200630/|url-status = live}}</ref> A 2008 report by the Swedish National Council for Crime Prevention finds evidence of discrimination towards individuals of foreign descent in the Swedish judicial system.<ref name=":23">{{Cite web|title = Diskriminering i rättsprocessen - Brå|url = https://www.bra.se/bra/publikationer/arkiv/publikationer/2008-02-21-diskriminering-i-rattsprocessen.html|website = www.bra.se|access-date = 2016-01-26|language = sv|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170317221242/http://bra.se/bra/publikationer/arkiv/publikationer/2008-02-21-diskriminering-i-rattsprocessen.html|archive-date = 2017-03-17}}</ref> The 2005 report finds that immigrants who entered Sweden during early childhood have lower crime rates than other immigrants.<ref name=":17">{{Cite web|title = Brottslighet bland personer födda i Sverige och i utlandet|url = https://www.bra.se/bra/publikationer/arkiv/publikationer/2005-12-14-brottslighet-bland-personer-fodda-i-sverige-och-i-utlandet.html|website = www.bra.se|access-date = 2016-01-26|language = sv|page = 10|archive-date = 17 January 2016|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160117174321/http://www.bra.se/bra/publikationer/arkiv/publikationer/2005-12-14-brottslighet-bland-personer-fodda-i-sverige-och-i-utlandet.html|url-status = live}}</ref> By taking account of socioeconomic factors (gender, age, education and income), the crime rate gap between immigrants and natives decreases.<ref name=":17" /> A 2013 study done by [[Stockholm University]] argued that designs like BRÅ 2005 may bias results by controlling for adult education and income, which may be influenced by prior offending.<ref name="gov">{{cite web|title=Facts about migration and crime in Sweden|date=23 February 2017|url=http://www.government.se/articles/2017/02/facts-about-migration-and-crime-in-sweden/|publisher=[[Government of Sweden]]|access-date=16 April 2017|archive-date=7 August 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220807044252/https://www.government.se/articles/2017/02/facts-about-migration-and-crime-in-sweden/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=":12" /> The authors furthermore found "that culture is unlikely to be a strong cause of crime among immigrants".<ref name=":12" />

A study published in 1997 attempted to explain the higher than average crime rates among immigrants to Sweden. It found that between 20 and 25 percent of asylum seekers to Sweden had experienced [[physical torture]], and many suffered from [[post-traumatic stress disorder]]. Other refugees had witnessed a close relative being killed.<ref name="tonry">{{cite journal|title= Ethnicity, Crime and Immigration: Comparative and Cross-National Perspectives|publisher=The University of Chicago Press|author= Michael Tonry|journal=[[Crime and Justice]]|page=24|year=1997}}</ref> The 2005 study reported that persons from [[North Africa]] and Western Asia were over-represented in crime statistics,<ref name=":16" /> whereas a 1997 paper additionally found immigrants from Finland, South America, Arab world and Eastern Europe to be over-represented in crime statistics.<ref name="tonry" /> Studies have found that native-born Swedes with high levels of unemployment are also over-represented in crime statistics.<ref name="politifact">{{cite web|author=Miriam Valverde|title=What the statistics say about Sweden, immigration and crime|url=http://www.politifact.com/truth-o-meter/article/2017/feb/20/what-statistics-say-about-immigration-and-sweden/|access-date=25 February 2017|archive-date=24 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170224170008/http://www.politifact.com/truth-o-meter/article/2017/feb/20/what-statistics-say-about-immigration-and-sweden/|url-status=live}}</ref>

A 1996 report by the Swedish National Council for Crime Prevention determined that between 1985 and 1989 individuals born in Iraq, North Africa (Algeria, Libya, Morocco and Tunisia), Africa (excluding Uganda and the North African countries), other Middle East (Jordan, Palestine, Syria), Iran and Eastern Europe (Romania, Bulgaria) were convicted of rape at rates 20, 23, 17, 9, 10 and 18 greater than individuals born in Sweden respectively.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.pdf-archive.com/2011/05/08/br-1996-2-invandrares-och-invandrares-barns-brottslighet-1/br-1996-2-invandrares-och-invandrares-barns-brottslighet-1.pdf |title=Invandrares och Invandrares Barns Brottslighet |access-date=2016-01-09 |archive-date=2017-02-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170225054413/https://www.pdf-archive.com/2011/05/08/br-1996-2-invandrares-och-invandrares-barns-brottslighet-1/br-1996-2-invandrares-och-invandrares-barns-brottslighet-1.pdf |page=107 |quote=Tabell 2.3. Participation, dvs. andelen personer som någon gång under femårsperioden 1985-1989 registrerats för brott i promille. Fördelad på födelseIand (Sverige omfattar personer födda i Sverige exklusive invandrares barn). Brottskategorierna mord, dråp våldtäkt övriga sexualbrott och rån...Våldtäkt - Sverige: 0.2, Irak: 4.0, Algeriet,Libyen,Marocko,Tunisien: 4.6, Övriga Afrika exkl. Uganda: 3.3, Jordanien,Palestina,Sytien: 1.9, Iran: 2.0, Rumänien,Bulgarien: 3.6}}</ref> A 2013 study argued that BRÅ 2005's reliance on adult education and income as controls was problematic, since those factors may themselves be affected by earlier offending, but it did not make the same criticism of the 1996 report.<ref name=":12" />

A 2013 study found that both first- and second-generation immigrants have a higher rate of suspected offenses than indigenous Swedes.<ref name=":11">{{Cite journal|title = Are Children of Immigrants Born in Sweden More Law-Abiding Than Immigrants? A Reconsideration |journal = Race and Justice|date = 2013-07-01|issn = 2153-3687|pages = 167–189|volume = 3|issue = 3|doi = 10.1177/2153368713486488|first1 = Johan|last1 = Kardell|first2 = Peter L.|last2 = Martens|s2cid = 154999783}}</ref> While first-generation immigrants have the highest offender rate, the offenders have the lowest average number of offenses, which indicates that there is a high rate of low-rate offending (many suspected offenders with only one single registered offense). The rate of chronic offending (offenders suspected of several offenses) is higher among indigenous Swedes than first-generation immigrants. Second-generation immigrants have higher rates of chronic offending than first-generation immigrants but lower total offender rates.<ref name=":11" />

===Switzerland===
{{further|Immigration to Switzerland|Crime in Switzerland#Immigrant criminality}}
In [[Switzerland]], 69.7% of the prison population did not have Swiss citizenship, compared to 22.1% of total resident population (as of 2008).
The figure of arrests by residence status is not usually made public. In 1997, when there were for the first time more foreigners than Swiss among the convicts under criminal law (out of a fraction of 20.6% of the total population at the time), a special report was compiled by the [[Federal Department of Justice and Police]] (published in 2001) which for the year 1998 found an arrest rate per 1000 adult population of 2.3 for Swiss citizens, 4.2 for legally resident aliens and 32 for asylum seekers. 21% of arrests made concerned individuals with no residence status, who were thus either ''[[sans papiers]]'' or "crime tourists" without any permanent residence in Switzerland.<ref name="Vimentis">{{cite web |title=Ausländerkriminalität in der Schweiz |url=http://www.vimentis.ch/d/publikation/154/Ausl%E4nderkriminalit%E4t+in+der+Schweiz.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090830061932/http://www.vimentis.ch/d/publikation/154/Ausl%E4nderkriminalit%E4t+in+der+Schweiz.html |archive-date=2009-08-30 |access-date=2009-10-01 |work=Vimentis}}</ref>{{Verify source|date=July 2024}}{{Update inline|date=July 2024}}

A 2019 study found that asylum seekers exposed to civil conflict and mass killing during childhood were 35% more prone to violent crimes than co-national asylum seekers who were not exposed to conflict.<ref name=":30">{{Cite journal|title=The Violent Legacy of Conflict: Evidence on Asylum Seekers, Crime, and Public Policy in Switzerland|journal=American Economic Review|volume=109|issue=12|pages=4378–4425|doi=10.1257/aer.20170263|year=2019|last1=Couttenier|first1=Mathieu|last2=Petrencu|first2=Veronica|last3=Rohner|first3=Dominic|last4=Thoenig|first4=Mathias|doi-access=free}}</ref> The conflict exposed cohorts have a higher propensity to target victims from their own nationality.<ref name=":30" /> Offering labor market access to the asylum seekers eliminates two-thirds of effect of conflict exposure on crime propensity.<ref name=":30" />

In 2010, a statistic was published which listed delinquency by nationality (based on 2009 data).
To avoid distortions due to demographic structure, only the male population aged between 18 and 34 was considered for each group. From the study, it became clear that crime rate is highly correlated on the country of origin of the various migrant groups.
Thus, immigrants from [[Germany]], [[France]] and [[Austria]] had a significantly lower crime rate than Swiss citizens (60% to 80%), while immigrants from [[Angola]], [[Nigeria]] and [[Algeria]] had a crime rate of above 600% of that of Swiss population.
In between these extremes were immigrants from [[Former Yugoslavia]], with crime rates of between 210% and 300% of the Swiss value.<ref>[http://www.tagesanzeiger.ch/schweiz/standard/Neue-Statistik-Tamilen-sind-krimineller-als-ExJugoslawen/story/27784193 Neue Statistik: Tamilen sind krimineller als Ex-Jugoslawen] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211208160650/https://www.tagesanzeiger.ch/schweiz/standard/neue-statistik-tamilen-sind-krimineller-als-exjugoslawen/story/27784193 |date=8 December 2021 }}, ''[[Tages-Anzeiger]]'' 12 September 2010.</ref>{{Verify source|date=July 2024}}

A 2023 study suggests that the increase in fear of immigrant crime in Switzerland was significantly impacted by potentially biased media coverage sensationalizing the issue.<ref name=":410" />

===Turkey===
A 2022 study has shown that [[Syrian refugees]] have no significant effect on crime rates in Turkey.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kayaoglu |first=Aysegul |date=2022 |title=Do refugees cause crime? |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0305750X22000481 |journal=World Development |language=en |volume=154 |article-number=105858 |doi=10.1016/j.worlddev.2022.105858 |s2cid=247302277 |issn=0305-750X |access-date=10 March 2022 |archive-date=10 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220310070357/https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0305750X22000481 |url-status=live |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

===United Kingdom===
{{See also|Modern immigration to the United Kingdom}}{{Primary sources section
| date = July 2024
}}
Historically, Irish immigrants to the United Kingdom in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries were considered over-represented amongst those appearing in court. Research suggests that policing strategy may have put immigrants at a disadvantage by targeting only the most public forms of crime, while locals were more likely able to engage in the types of crimes that could be conducted behind locked doors.<ref>{{Cite journal|title = How Criminal were the Irish? Bias in the Detection of London Currency Crime, 1797–1821 |journal = The London Journal|volume = 43|pages = 36–52|date = 2017-02-09|doi = 10.1080/03058034.2016.1270876|first = Adam|last = Crymble|doi-access = free|hdl = 2299/19710|hdl-access = free}}</ref> An analysis of historical courtroom records suggests that despite higher rates of arrest, immigrants were not systematically disadvantaged by the British court system in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.<ref>King, Peter. ''Ethnicity, Prejudice, and Justice: The Treatment of the Irish at the Old Bailey, 1750–1825'', Journal of British Studies, Volume 52, Issue 2, April 2013, pp. 390–414</ref>

On 30 June 2022 there were 9,682 prisoners from 164 different countries in the jails of England and Wales.<ref name=":9">{{Cite web|url = http://researchbriefings.files.parliament.uk/documents/SN04334/SN04334.pdf|title = Prison Population Statistics from the UK Parliament|access-date = 12 January 2016|archive-date = 29 March 2017|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170329021406/http://researchbriefings.files.parliament.uk/documents/SN04334/SN04334.pdf|url-status = live}}</ref> Albania, Poland and Romania formed the highest percentage of foreign nationals in UK prisons.<ref name=":9" /> In total, foreigners represented 12% of the prison population,<ref name=":9" /> whereas foreign nationals are 13% of the total population in England and Wales.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Immigration Patterns of Non-UK Born Populations in England and Wales in 2011 |url=http://www.ons.gov.uk/ons/dcp171776_346219.pdf |access-date=11 January 2016 |archive-date=9 January 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160109180755/http://www.ons.gov.uk/ons/dcp171776_346219.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref> During the 2000s, there was a 111% increase of foreign nationals in UK prisons.<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|title = Foreign National Prisoners in the UK: Explanations and Implications|journal = The Howard Journal of Criminal Justice|date = 2011-05-01|issn = 1468-2311|pages = 184–198|volume = 50|issue = 2|doi = 10.1111/j.1468-2311.2010.00655.x|first = James|last = Banks|s2cid = 142989045|url = http://shura.shu.ac.uk/6803/1/Banks_Foreign_National_Prisoners.pdf|access-date = 18 August 2019|archive-date = 20 July 2018|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20180720054132/http://shura.shu.ac.uk/6803/1/Banks_Foreign_National_Prisoners.pdf|url-status = live}}</ref> According to one study, "there is little evidence to support the theory that the foreign national prison population continues to grow because foreign nationals are more likely to commit crime than are British citizens or more likely to commit crime of a serious nature".<ref name=":2" /> The increase may partly be due to the disproportionate number of convicted for drug offences; crimes associated with illegal immigration (fraud and forgery of government documents, and immigration offenses); ineffective deportation provisions; and a lack of viable options to custody (which affects bail and sentencing decision making).<ref name=":2" />

Research has found no evidence of an average causal impact of immigration on crime in the United Kingdom.<ref name="NewEvidence"/><ref name=":4abc" /><ref name=":2" /> One study based on evidence from England and Wales in the 2000s found no evidence of an average causal impact of immigration on crime in England and Wales.<ref name="NewEvidence" /> No causal impact and no immigrant differences in the likelihood of being arrested were found for London, which saw large immigration changes.<ref name="NewEvidence" /> A 2017 study offered qualified support for the notion that immigration had contributed to declining crime rates in the UK.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ignatans|first1=Dainis|last2=Matthews|first2=Roger|date=2017-07-20|title=Immigration and the Crime Drop|url=https://brill.com/view/journals/eccl/25/3/article-p205_205.xml|journal=European Journal of Crime, Criminal Law and Criminal Justice|language=en|volume=25|issue=3|pages=205–229|doi=10.1163/15718174-02503002|s2cid=151811010|issn=1571-8174|access-date=31 January 2021|archive-date=7 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210207015726/https://brill.com/view/journals/eccl/25/3/article-p205_205.xml|url-status=live}}</ref> A study of two large waves of immigration to the UK (the late 1990s/early 2000s asylum seekers and the post-2004 inflow from EU accession countries) found that the "first wave led to a modest but significant rise in property crime, while the second wave had a small negative impact. There was no effect on violent crime; arrest rates were not different, and changes in crime cannot be ascribed to crimes against immigrants. The findings are consistent with the notion that differences in labor market opportunities of different migrant groups shape their potential impact on crime."<ref name=":4abc"/> A 2013 study found "that crime is significantly lower in those neighborhoods with sizeable immigrant population shares" and that "the crime reducing effect is substantially enhanced if the enclave is composed of immigrants from the same ethnic background."<ref name=":6"/> A 2014 study of property crimes based on the Crime and Justice Survey (CJS) of 2003, (a national representative survey where respondents in England and Wales were asked questions regarding their criminal activities), after taking into account the [[under-reporting]] of crimes, even found that "immigrants who are located in London and black immigrants are significantly less criminally active than their native counterparts".<ref name=":8" /> Another 2014 study found that "areas that have witnessed the greatest percentage of recent immigrants arriving since 2004 have not witnessed higher levels of robbery, violence, or sex offending" but have "experienced higher levels of drug offenses."<ref>{{Cite journal|title = Reevaluating the Effect of Recent Immigration on Crime Estimating the Impact of Change in Discrete Migration Flows to the United Kingdom Following EU Accession |journal = Crime & Delinquency|volume = 62|issue = 11|date = 2014-07-15|issn = 0011-1287|pages = 1426–1447|doi = 10.1177/0011128714542500|first = Richard|last = Stansfield|s2cid = 142996587}}</ref>

A 2008 study found that the crime rate of Eastern European immigrants was the same as that of the indigenous population.<ref>Johnston, Phillip. [https://web.archive.org/web/20090904151942/http://blogs.telegraph.co.uk/news/philipjohnston/3674251/Immigration_and_crime_the_real_results/ "Immigration and crime: the real results"]. ''[[The Daily Telegraph]]''. 16 April 2008. Accessed 21 September 2011.</ref>

An analysis of data by ''[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]]'' in 2024 found that the overall imprisonment rate of foreign nationals was 27 per cent higher than for British citizens.<ref>{{cite news |title=Revealed: First migrant crime table |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2024/10/04/one-in-50-albanians-uk-in-prison-telegraph-analysis/#:~:text=The%20analysis%20suggests%20that%20the,least%20likely%20to%20be%20jailed. |website=[[The Daily Telegraph]] | date=4 October 2024 |access-date=9 October 2024 | last1=Hymas | first1=Charles | last2=Butcher | first2=Ben }}</ref> A 2025 analysis by the Centre for Migration Control, an anti-immigration think tank, found that non-British citizens were around 3.5 times more likely than British citizens to be arrested for sexual offenses.<ref name="u278">{{cite web | last=Dathan | first=Matt | title=Foreign citizens 3.5 times more likely to be arrested for sex crimes | website=The Times and The Sunday Times | date=2025-01-07 | url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/crime/article/foreign-citizens-35-times-more-likely-to-be-arrested-for-sex-crimes-fnhxgr3wk | access-date=2025-03-10}}</ref>

According to the data from the Ministry of Justice, obtained under freedom of information laws, foreign nationals have disproportionately committed sex crimes between 2021 and 2023. Afghans and Eritreans – were more than 20 times more likely to account for sexual offence convictions than British citizens, according to the data. Overall, foreign nationals were 71 per cent more likely than Britons to be responsible for sex crime convictions. In terms of overall crime nationals from Albania topped the crime league table; followed by Moldova, Congo, Namibia and Somalia.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hymas |first=Charles |date=2025-03-10 |title=Foreigners convicted of nearly a quarter of sex crimes |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2025/03/10/foreigners-commit-up-to-quarter-of-sex-crimes/ |access-date=2025-03-10 |work=The Telegraph |language=en-GB |issn=0307-1235}}</ref>

Official GOV.UK data for the period of April 2022 to March 2023 has the arrest rate for White British at 9.2 per every 1,000 people. This compares to 2.8 for Chinese, 11.3 for Pakistani, 22.7 for Black Caribbean, and 52.4 for Black other.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-07-03 |title=Arrests |url=https://www.ethnicity-facts-figures.service.gov.uk/crime-justice-and-the-law/policing/number-of-arrests/latest/ |access-date=2025-07-27 |website=www.ethnicity-facts-figures.service.gov.uk |language=en}}</ref>

Data from the Ministry of Justice (MoJ), drawn from the Police National Computer and obtained under freedom of information laws, showed that 26 per cent of the 1,453 sex assault convictions on women in 2024 were accounted for by foreign nationals. A further 8 per cent were committed by offenders of "unknown" nationalities, a category which will include some foreign nationals, meaning the overall proportion could be higher.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Hymas |first1=Charles |last2=Riley-Smith |first2=Ben |date=2025-06-18 |title=Foreign nationals convicted of quarter of sex assaults on women |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2025/06/18/foreign-nationals-convicted-quarter-of-sex-assaults-women/ |access-date=2025-07-27 |work=The Telegraph |language=en-GB |issn=0307-1235}}</ref>

A House of Commons report from July 2024 shows that foreign nationals make up 10% of the prison population, form over 168 countries, with the largest section being those born within EEA European countries.<ref>{{Cite web| title=Prison Population Statistics | url=https://researchbriefings.files.parliament.uk/documents/SN04334/SN04334.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150614180433/http://researchbriefings.files.parliament.uk/documents/SN04334/SN04334.pdf | archive-date=2015-06-14}}</ref>

Criminals from just three countries account for 40 per cent of foreign prisoners in Scotland's jails, according to analysis of official figures via Scottish Prison Service (SPS) data. Just over four in 10 of the total were from just three countries – Albania, Poland and Vietnam. More than a quarter (26.3 per cent) of Eritreans living in Scotland are estimated to be in prison and more than one in five (21.9 per cent) Somalians. Almost one in six Albanians (15.8 per cent) and Vietnamese (15.2 per cent) people living in Scotland are estimated to be imprisoned, according to comparison of census and SPS data.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Johnson |first=Simon |date=2025-07-30 |title=Almost half of Scotland's foreign prisoners come from just three countries |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/politics/2025/07/30/half-scotlands-foreign-prisoners-from-just-three-countries/ |access-date=2025-08-01 |work=The Telegraph |language=en-GB |issn=0307-1235}}</ref>

==Americas==
=== Canada ===
A 2014 study found that immigration reduced the property crime rate in Canada: "new immigrants do not have a significant impact on property crime rates, but as they stay longer, more established immigrants actually decrease property crime rates significantly."<ref name=":24">{{Cite web|title = Immigration and Crime: Evidence from Canada|url = http://www.clsrn.econ.ubc.ca/workingpapers/CLSRN%20Working%20Paper%20no.%20135%20-%20Zhang.pdf|publisher = Vancouver School of Economics|date = 2014-01-01|first = Haimin|last = Zhang|access-date = 11 July 2016|archive-date = 17 May 2017|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170517080849/http://www.clsrn.econ.ubc.ca/workingpapers/CLSRN%20Working%20Paper%20no.%20135%20-%20Zhang.pdf}}</ref>

=== Chile ===
A 2020 study found no relationship between immigration and crime in Chile.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Leiva|first1=Mauricio|last2=Vasquez-Lavín|first2=Felipe|last3=Ponce Oliva|first3=Roberto D.|date=2020-02-01|title=Do immigrants increase crime? Spatial analysis in a middle-income country|journal=World Development|volume=126|article-number=104728|doi=10.1016/j.worlddev.2019.104728|s2cid=211465409|issn=0305-750X}}</ref> A 2023 study found media competition as a possible driver of the increasing fear of immigrant crime despite crime not increasing.<ref name=":410" /><ref name=":68" />

===United States===
{{further|Illegal immigration to the United States and crime}}
